body: I've only had a chance to skim the rule source, but I think I agree this is a bug. The rule is looking at built-in global names without using scope analysis to determine if a global scope reference is even being modified (which it clearly isn't in the example case).
I'll try to repro when I get on my laptop, and I'll try to get a fix in sometime this weekend.
If `Set` is declared at the top level, wouldn't this result in reassigning the global?

@not-an-aardvark Yes, but since this is in a module, it is scoped to the module function scope.  In my fork I changed the name to `MigrationSet` because I agree that it is better to just avoid the issue altogether, but if I had left it as `Set`, it would mean you cannot access the global `Set` inside that module.

Sure, but that's not what this rule is for. This rule is about extending
the prototype of built-in objects. Also, in a Node module, no, it wouldn't
reassign the global.

Update: I'm about halfway through rewriting the rule to use eslint-scope to do scope analysis, but I got quite busy over the weekend. I'm hoping to have a fix for this in time for this week's planned alpha release on Friday.
Wow, awesomely quick turn around on this.  Thanks @platinumazure!!
@wesleytodd Save your thanks until I can finish the job :smile:
Update: No meaningful updates, been busy the last few days. Unfortunately this won't make tomorrow's release, but it'll get in before 4.0.0 is out.

**What changes did you make? (Give an overview)**

Rewrote the rule to use eslint-scope references to find violations of this rule. Previously, a prototype extension would be reported if the name of the owning object was the same as a builtin with uppercase first letter; now it only reports actual references to builtins with uppercase first letter.

**Is there anything you'd like reviewers to focus on?**

* I marked this as Update because I basically rewrote the rule.
* The rule relies on the fact that we add [the builtin environment's variables](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/master/lib/eslint.js#L169) to the [eslint-scope global scope](https://github.com/eslint/eslint/blob/master/lib/eslint.js#L186-L196).
